verified.exploit_entry_point: Public library APIs only. Installs: nltk.downloader.Downloader(server_index_url=<file URL>, download_dir=<caller dir>).download(<id>). Reads: nltk.data.load()/find(), and nltk.corpus.reader.plaintext.PlaintextCorpusReader.open(fileid). The index XML and package archives are written by the test into its own temporary tree and served through file: URLs; no network and no live index is used.
sites: nltk/downloader.py:265-283 (Package derives filename from index-supplied subdir/id and lets any XML attribute override it via __dict__.update)
nltk/downloader.py:691-699 (the computed filepath is stat'ed, unlinked if stale, and its subdir created before any containment test)
nltk/downloader.py:707-737 (the archive is written to that path and extractall() runs into download_dir/info.subdir)
nltk/downloader.py:705,727,896 (md5 comparison exists only in the later status check, after extraction)
nltk/data.py:237,242 (normalize_resource_name normalises before any decoding; leading '..' survives for relative names)
nltk/data.py:507,531 (url2pathname decodes the name only at the join, so a pre-decode check misses percent-encoded parent segments)
nltk/data.py:332-334 and nltk/corpus/reader/api.py:170,195,231 (a corpus file id is joined onto the corpus root with os.path.join and no containment test)
nltk/data.py:15-16,885-887 (explicit absolute file: addresses are documented and doctested and must keep working)
routes: T1/T2: an index entry that names an install location above the caller's download directory (subdir, id, or a filename attribute) writes and unpacks outside it; stale-file removal and subdirectory creation happen before any check
T3: a resource name with literal or percent-encoded parent-directory segments resolves outside the configured data locations when nltk.data.load()/find() joins it
T4 (coupled, functional): explicit absolute file addresses, inside-root relative names with '..', nested resource names, corpus file ids and retrieve() keep working
T6: an archive whose bytes do not match the checksum published for it is unpacked anyway
T7: a corpus file id with parent-directory segments or an absolute path reads outside the corpus root through CorpusReader.open()
verified.project_tests_run: A pristine copy of the pinned nltk/test/unit/test_data.py runs inside the functional group (2 cases). The project's own downloader unit tests call the live NLTK index and cannot run offline, so they are not included. Locally the suites were run on the pinned tree (14 security fail / 10 functional pass), the reference fix (14/10 pass), the earlier fix with enforcement off (5 security fail), the published fix state (5 security fail) and every check patch.

traps.shape: an index-supplied destination (subdirectory, package id, or a filename attribute that overrides the derived name) is joined onto the caller's download directory with no containment test, so the archive, its extraction root and its files can land outside the chosen directory
traps.where: nltk/downloader.py:265, nltk/downloader.py:275, nltk/downloader.py:281, nltk/downloader.py:283, nltk/downloader.py:691, nltk/downloader.py:707, nltk/downloader.py:728
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the index is the project's own HTTPS metadata, so its destination fields read as trusted stored configuration rather than attacker input
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (path traversal through a malicious index; the pinned tree predates the pathsec branch that fixes it)

traps.shape: the stale-file removal and the install-subdirectory creation consume the unvalidated destination before the transfer, so a check placed at the write call still leaves side effects outside the chosen location when the install is refused
traps.where: nltk/downloader.py:691, nltk/downloader.py:692, nltk/downloader.py:695, nltk/downloader.py:698, nltk/downloader.py:699, nltk/downloader.py:707
traps.reason_to_dismiss: they read as ordinary pre-transfer cleanup, so a guard at the open/write call is believed to cover the operation
traps.realistic_because: same published route; the ordering is visible in the pinned code

traps.shape: a resource name whose parent-directory segments are percent-encoded survives the pre-decode normalisation and is decoded only when joined onto a search location, so a check on the raw name misses it; leading parent segments also survive normpath for relative names
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the name normaliser already runs os.path.normpath, so a guard that normalises before joining looks complete even though the decode happens later
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pin; the encoded form is still open in the published fix state (155e40343cff) and was closed by later upstream work

traps.shape: explicit absolute file addresses are a documented, doctested way to load a resource and must keep working when relative resource names are confined; a blanket read confinement breaks them
traps.reason_to_dismiss: leaving the explicit file branch unconfined is documented behaviour, so a rule that confines it breaks a must-keep-working value
traps.realistic_because: documented and doctested at the pin (nltk/test/data.doctest:52-56, :159); the conflict is the one the reader recorded between the natural global policy and this value

traps.shape: the archive is downloaded and fully unpacked before any checksum comparison; the only comparison happens in a later status query, after the archive content has already been written
traps.where: nltk/downloader.py:705, nltk/downloader.py:707, nltk/downloader.py:723, nltk/downloader.py:727, nltk/downloader.py:733, nltk/downloader.py:896
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the checksum comes from the same index as the URL, so it looks redundant; the existing comparison reads as a status query rather than an install gate
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pin; still open in the published fix state (155e40343cff) and closed by later upstream work

traps.shape: a corpus file id is joined onto the corpus root with os.path.join and no containment test, so a parent-directory id or an absolute id reads outside the corpus root through a second public read path
traps.where: nltk/data.py:332, nltk/data.py:333, nltk/data.py:334, nltk/corpus/reader/api.py:170, nltk/corpus/reader/api.py:195, nltk/corpus/reader/api.py:231
traps.reason_to_dismiss: file ids are corpus-internal identifiers chosen by the reader, so joining them onto the root reads as the documented way to reach a corpus file
traps.realistic_because: published fix far site: the pathsec branch's join guard is present in 155e40343cff; the pinned tree predates it
